newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 2.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.

- The Ulster police force has begun an investigation into an incident in which armed and masked members of the Irish Republican Army (IRA) appeared on the streets of Belfast on Tuesday afternoon in a rare public display.

- Over 560 million Irish pounds was wiped off the value of the Irish stock market on Tuesday as investors reacted negatively to heavy falls in U.S. share prices and the expectation that the U.S. market will fall further before it stabilises.
- Shane Broderick, the 22-year-old jockey who suffered a severe fall at Fairyhouse on Monday, is in a critical condition in the intensive care unit at the Mater Hospital.

- Irish police have recaptured the 15-year-old self-proclaimed 'young general' who went on the run over the Easter holiday period after orchestrating a riot which left Irish police force members injured, a number of cars wrecked and residents terrified.
- Irish owners of shares watched anxiously on Tuesday to see if an attempted rally on Wall Street would hold.

- Income and profits at Ireland's stockbroking firms look set to plummet following confirmation on Tuesday that the commission fee charged to institutional shareholders for share deals has been cut sharply by the larger brokers.
- Irish employer and employee pension fund contributors were among the big losers in Tuesday's fall in the Irish stock market.

- Irish troops are set to serve under a NATO-led command for the first time ever if the Irish government backs a proposal from the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Dick Spring, which threatened at one stage to fall victim to coalition neutrality divisions.
